verdict.rationale: LiteLLM supports rule-like automated responses to specific system events — automatic fallback/retry when a call fails ([litellm-docs-4],[litellm-docs-21],[litellm-docs-22]), content-policy-violation fallbacks ([litellm-docs-18]), and budget/spend limits that cap or block usage when a threshold is hit ([litellm-docs-25],[litellm-docs-35],[litellm-docs-7]). This is real event→action automation, but it's confined to a fixed set of built-in event types (failures, budget, rate limits) rather than a general user-definable rules/trigger engine for arbitrary events and actions. Missing for 10: a generic 'if X event then Y action' rules engine/webhook trigger system, user-defined custom event types, and independent evidence of this automation working reliably in production.
